Expressions
Overview
Expressions are the core computational units of Scaly. Every expression evaluates to a value. An operation is a sequence of operands; operators are ordinary identifiers rather than built-in keywords. When operators are chained, they combine according to standard mathematical precedence (multiplicative binds tighter than additive, which binds tighter than comparison). Prefix forms and parentheses provide explicit control where needed.

If Expressions
If expressions evaluate one of two branches based on a boolean condition. The syntax is if followed by the condition, a colon, the consequent, and optionally else with an alternative. if true: 1 else 0 ; evaluates to 1 if false: 1 else 0 ; evaluates to 0 if 5 > 3: 10 else 20 ; evaluates to 10
If expressions can be nested: if false: 1 else if true: 2 else 3 ; evaluates to 2
Match Expressions
A match expression — comparing a value against multiple case alternatives — is part of the grammar but not yet functional in the current compiler. Use if/else chains, or choose on a union, instead.
